controlled_assignment.concept: Obsidian-petal resonance fitting in a volcanic-glass kinetic couture atelier

prompt.prompt_en: Create a photorealistic portrait in a volcanic-glass kinetic couture atelier. An unmistakably adult woman with long dark wavy hair tests the opening cycle of an articulated obsidian-petal cape while a technician adjusts rear brass linkages. She faces camera with a neutral, minimally expressive look. Her heart-shaped face is primary: the complete forehead temple cheek jaw and chin perimeter remains visible; the face length-to-width relation remains visible; the forehead and upper temples are wider than the jaw; the lower cheeks and jaw narrow continuously toward a narrow chin; a widow's peak remains optional while anatomical widths stay readable. Sweep hair from both temples, cheek edges, jaw corners, and chin. A symmetrical waist-up framing keeps both face outlines and the shoulder machinery in one focal plane. Use restrained low-distortion portrait perspective and soft frontal facial-shaping light. Fine glass dust and worn tools retain tactile documentary texture. Warm furnace reflections skim only obsidian edges; her face stays softly modeled.
prompt.negative_en: body distortion, broken facial features, distorted fingers, excessive HDR, illustration look, plastic-looking skin, fake-looking background, over-processed retouching, 3D render look

hard_gates.evidence: Dark side hair crosses both upper-temple boundaries and merges into the cheek contour, masking the complete width transition.
The center hairline-to-chin span and exposed upper-face breadth remain readable together in the frontal view.
The exposed forehead and upper-temple skin span is visibly broader than the mandibular angle span.
The lower cheeks narrow only modestly into a broad rounded chin, so continuous taper to a narrow chin is absent.
Exposed anatomical skin boundaries under even light carry the hierarchy rather than iconography, makeup, shadow, or lens effects.
